name: Gemini 3.8 Flash TTS
access: Gemini API (Interactions API and generateContent; REST and SDKs)

Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (the model card lists it and the launch post said coming soon; Google Cloud's Text-to-Speech page says the 3.8 models are in Preview through the Gemini Enterprise API only, and not through the Cloud Text-to-Speech API)

voice.input_audio: none: the model takes text only. Each text block can carry a speech_metadata annotation (style and speaker) and inline angle-bracket tags. Reference audio goes only to the Voices API, to make a replicated voice [g-tts-guide] [g-voice-repl]
voice.output_audio: WAV (audio/wav, 16-bit signed PCM, mono, 24 kHz) by default on a unary request; headerless raw PCM (audio/l16, 24 kHz) by default on a streaming request. audio/mulaw and audio/alaw (8-bit G.711) can be requested, and sample_rate can be set, for example to 24000, 16000 or 8000 [g-tts-guide]. Google marks all output with a SynthID watermark [g-blog-38]
voice.voices: custom cloning and voice design: 30 prebuilt studio voices; an Extended Voice Library (the guide says hundreds of voices, the launch post says 2,000+); voice design from a text description; voice replication from a 10 to 30 second reference clip plus a consent clip; 200 stored custom voices per project [g-tts-guide] [g-voice-design] [g-voice-repl] [g-blog-38]
languages: 130+ languages, with automatic detection of the input language; the model page lists them [g-model-flash-page] [g-tts-guide]
voice.turn_detection: none: a synthesis model. In a multi-speaker request every turn names its speaker in speech_metadata, and that is the only turn boundary [g-tts-guide]
voice.interruption: Not a conversation model. The pages read describe no barge-in or cancel message; the client stops playback (inferred) [g-tts-guide]
voice.latency: Google publishes no time-to-first-audio figure. Artificial Analysis reports a median of 48.8 characters generated per second (throughput, not latency) [aa-g38]. Google calls Flash-Lite the low-latency choice and Flash the fidelity choice [g-model-flash-page]
voice.session_limit: Input up to 8,192 tokens and output up to 16,384 tokens per request on the Gemini API; the model card gives 8K text in and 64K tokens of audio out [g-model-flash-page] [g-card-38]. At 25 audio tokens a second, 16,384 tokens is about 11 minutes of speech (computed; Google's Cloud Text-to-Speech page gives about 655 seconds as the output cap of its 16,384-token Gemini-TTS models) [g-cloud-tts]. A single request takes at most 2 speakers, and they must use prebuilt voices [g-tts-guide]

pricing_usd_per_mtok.notes: Per token, Gemini API Standard tier, paid plan [g-pricing]. The input field is the text rate and the output field is the audio rate. Both rates are promotional until 2026-12-31 and double on 2027-01-01: text in US$0.50 then US$1.00, audio out US$9.00 then US$18.00 per Mtok. Audio counts 25 tokens a second, so the audio rate is about US$0.00225 per 10 seconds of speech until the change. Cached input is US$0.125 then US$0.25. Batch and Flex cost half of Standard, and a Priority tier exists. The free tier costs nothing and Google can use its data to improve products; the paid tier is not used for that. Artificial Analysis converts the price to US$16.5 per 1M characters [aa-pv].
